summary: Wilhelm von Humboldt (1767–1835) worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Viadrina, Göttingen, and Jena under Campe, Engel, Dohm, Klein, Lichtenberg, Heyne, and Chézy. He founded Humboldt University of Berlin and held a post there around 1809–1810.
Will B. Miller is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Janet Gyatso, and he also studied under Lopen Chorten in 2012.

Will Sweetman is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1989–1992) and Lancaster University (~1993–1996), and held a post at the University of Otago around 2004.

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby (1933–2003) was a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard. His career included teaching posts at McGill, Yale, and Trinity College, Toronto, before becoming founding director at Toronto.
Willard J. Peterson (b. 1939) is a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. Mentored by Denis Twitchett, he served as a professor at Princeton University, where his post was attested in 1981.

Willard Van Orman Quine (1908–2000) was a philosopher and linguist. Educated at Oberlin College and Harvard University, he served as an assistant professor at Harvard (1940–1978) and held visiting posts at Wesleyan and Oxford.

Willem Bollée (1927–2020) was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University and the University of Hamburg. He served as assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and later as lecturer and professor at Heidelberg University (~1977–1993).

Willem Caland (1859–1932) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at Leiden University, studying under Carel Gabriel Cobet and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1906–1929) and a post at Leiden.

Willem van der Molen (b. 1952) is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1971–1983) and held posts at Leiden University (~1983) and the University of Indonesia.
William Blackstone (1723–1780) studied at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College (~1738–1745). He subsequently held a post at the University of Oxford from around 1753 to 1766.

William C. Chittick (b. 1943) works in religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tehran (~1966–1974) and held posts at Sharif University of Technology, University at Albany, SUNY, and Stony Brook University.

William C. Kirby (b. 1950) is a Sinologist and historian. He studied at Dartmouth and Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn. He was professor and dean at Washington University in St. Louis (~1980–1992) before becoming a dean at Harvard (~1992).

William Carey (1761–1834) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ramram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. He was appointed Professor of Sanscrit, &c. at Fort William College in 1801 and co-founded Serampore College.

William Dwight Whitney (1827–1894) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Williams College, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, Roth, and Bopp. He held a professorship in Sanskrit at Yale from 1853 to 1894.

William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held academic posts at Colby College (attested 2007), Marlboro College (attested 2013), and the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

William Edward Soothill (1861–1935) was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of London, he served as President of Shanxi University in 1911 and became Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford in 1920.

William Erskine (1773–1852) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and studied at the University of Edinburgh from approximately 1787 to 1792.
William Evans Hoyle (1855–1926) studied at the University of Manchester from approximately 1872 to 1874 and subsequently continued his studies at Christ Church from around 1874 to 1877.
William Frederic Sinclair (d. 1900) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He was educated at the Royal School, Armagh, and entered a post with the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. (b. 1943) is a Sinologist educated at Indiana University and Bonn, studying under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. He served as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, holding the Halls-Bascom chair from 1995.
